answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a costly, slowly maturing reputation bond before it can earn: like a sable guarding its grove, a new agent must first do verifiable useful work and lock a deposit that only unlocks after sustained honest service, while a pearl of earned trust grows with each attested task. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits plus a thousand histories, so the attacker pays real work and capital per identity while honest agents amortize one bond over a long career.
